chunks.arabic_text: القَّاسِمُ بْنُ الرَّبِيعَ، الصَّحَّافُ، كَوْفِيٌّ. ضَعِيفٌ فِي حَدِيثِهِ، غَالٍ فِي مَذْهَبِهِ، لَا إِلْفَاتَ إِلَيْهِ، وَلَا ارْتِفَاعَ بِهِ.

translations.en: Al-Qāsim ibn al-Rabīʿ, al-Ṣaḥḥāf. Kufan. Weak in his ḥadīth, a ghālī in his madhhab, he is not turned to, and there is no ascending by him.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿāf* critiques Al-Qāsim ibn al-Rabīʿ, a Kufan narrator, for his weakness in hadith transmission and his tendency toward exaggeration (ghulūw) in his theological school, rendering him unreliable for deriving religious rulings. His classification highlights the critical Shia methodology of evaluating narrators not only for textual accuracy but also for doctrinal fidelity, ensuring that the chain of transmission preserves both the letter and spirit of the Imams' teachings.
en.seo_question: Who is Al-Qāsim ibn al-Rabīʿ al-Ṣaḥḥāf and what is his status in hadith sciences?
